newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria cracks down on fuel smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria cracks down on fuel smuggling.

text.p: Bulgarian security forces have stepped up controls on the border with Macedonia to prevent smuggling of scarce fuel, officials said on Wednesday.

"We have turned back tonnes of fuel from the border. Now we have five trucks loaded with 93 tonnes of fuel oil which will be returned to their owner in Varna," said Oleg Petrov, chief of the economic police at the regional interior affairs directorate in the town of Kyustendil.
Bulgaria's new interim government, which inherited crippling fuel and grain shortages, has banned fuel exports until April 30, but prices are higher in neighbouring countries.
Apart from fuel, exports of foodstuffs, tobacco, medicines and some other goods were been banned last week.
"The effect of the ban was almost immediate and traffic, including visiting Macedonians, sharply fell," Petrov told Reuters.
Security forces inspect vehicles at a new checkpoint before they go through the usual customs checks.
Up to 700 vehicles a day were crossing through the Gjueshevo checkpoint before controls were tightened, and their number has now dropped by one third, officials said.
The interior ministry said it had stepped up checks on other crossing points and border police had prevented the export of fuel, food and medicine to Yugoslavia and Turkey.
Petrov said vehicles could cross the border only with the petrol in their tank and any with more than one tank or with specially enlarged tanks was returned.
One driver waiting with some 20 trucks and 20 cars to cross the border said workmen in the nearby town of Kyustendil were able to build extra fuel tanks for trucks and cars.
Bulgarians carry goods to the nearest Macedonian markets and Macedonians shop in Kyustendil to boost trade back home, officials said.
"I have been trading in contraband for the last five years with everyday goods and that's how I feed my family," said one middle-aged man, driving an old Ford.
"But I have never been in the petrol business and controls have not affected my trips," he said.
Bulgaria is suffering severe petrol shortages caused by a shortage of hard currency to pay for crude supplies, but petrol is still cheaper than in Macedonia.

Most petrol stations are closed and municipalities are distributing precious stocks of petrol and diesel only for ambulances, food delivery trucks, the police, the army and other social services, officials said.

Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery, Neftochim, which supplies almost the whole domestic market, said on Wednesday it had increased refining volumes to 12,000 tonnes of crude from some 8,000 tonnes last week and 22,000 tonnes in December.

The debt-ridden refinery, which has 116,000 tonnes of crude in storage, now distributes 1,700 tonnes of gasoline and 2,300 tonnes of diesel from 850-1,000 tonnes last week, following a drastic hike of fuel prices by up to 178 percent.
